# ND-100

ND-100 (3033S / 3033E-CX), 48 bits stored in 64, ROM storage form

- **Name for `%#MODEL` and the settings:** `nd100`
- **Also accepted:** `nd-100`
- **Word width in the bit view:** 64 bits
- **Image written by *Assemble*:** .CODE, 10-byte records
- **Ending of the image file:** `.CODE`
- **Mnemonics:** 299
- **Colours shared with:** ND-100, ND-110 and ND-120
- **Definitions:** [`defs/tokens/nd100-tokens.yaml`](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/nd-microcode-meta/blob/main/defs/tokens/nd100-tokens.yaml)

## How the bits are given

The word is four groups of 16 bits: `w4` (bits 63-48), `w3` (47-32), `w2` (31-16) and `w1` (15-0), each written as 6 octal digits. Groups that are all zero are left out of the tables below. A mnemonic sets the bits that are 1 in its groups; the mnemonics of one instruction are ORed together.

## Fields of the word

The fields below are the ones this variant defines itself. The other fields are those of `nd110-fields.yaml`; see the page of that variant.

| Field | Bits | Width | Description | Used when | Default |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| `TC` | 21:20 | 2 | Cycle-length selector. Two timing bits combined into a single 4-value field: 00 = FAST 01 = NORM 10 = SLOW 11 = WAIT |  | 2 |
| `VECT0` | 25 | 1 | Inverted VECT. When 0 (active), the lower 4 bits of the branch target are taken from one of IR / ALD / RA (selected by MIS) instead of from PROM bits 0:3. When 1 (inactive), PROM supplies all 12 bits of the branch target. |  | 1 |
| `SLWCS0` | 26 | 1 | Inverted slow-CS / WCS-load enable. When 0 (active), initiates START LOAD WRITABLE CS regardless of VECT0/MAPJ0 - the current microinstruction loads the writable control store instead of branching normally. |  | 1 |
| `MAPJ0` | 27 | 1 | Inverted map-jump enable. When 0 (active) with SLWCS0=1 and VECT0=1, dispatches to the macro-opcode decode-PLA address for the current macroinstruction (or to the interrupt vector entry if /INT RQ is asserted). |  | 1 |
| `IDBS` | 40:37 | 4 | Internal Data Bus Source - 4-bit selector. |  | 0 |
| `SEXT` | 41 | 1 | Sign-Extend modifier for the IDBS source. When set (together with IDBS = GPR, which is the primary documented use case), the GPR value is sign-extended from bit 7 to bits 8-15 as it is latched onto the IDB. This eases address-calculation and argument-instruction code paths. |  | 0 |
| `MIS` | 43:42 | 2 | Two-bit multi-role field. All three roles are confirmed on ND-100: (a) Shift mode when ALUM = 11 (shift instruction): 00 = ASH (arithmetic shift) 01 = ROT (rotational shift) 10 = ZIN (zero-end-input shift) 11 = LIR (link-end-input shift) (b) Page mode on memory-op COMMs (EXRQ/IRDRQ/DERQ/RDRQ/WRRQ): 00 = fetch / physical address (no paging) 01 = PT (normal page table) 10 = APT (alternative page table) 11 = HOLD (last-used page table) (c) Lower-4-bits source for vectored jumps (VECT0=0): 00 = IR(0..3) (used by TRA, TRR) 01 = IR(8..10) (used in memory-reference addr calc) 10 = ALD(0..3) 11 = A-operand bits All three roles share the same two bits; the active role is determined by the other fields (ALUM, COMM, VECT0) of the same microinstruction. |  | 0 |
| `EN_EXT` | 50 | 1 | Enable Extended register file. Same function as XRF on ND-110; renamed for ND-110. |  | 0 |

    ```yaml
    # ==================================================================
    ```

    ```yaml
    # carry-in trio. The w4 octal values below correspond directly to
    # the user's authoritative assembler output. Many of these match
    ```

| Mnemonic | Bits | Description | Notes |

| `LCOUNT` | `000100` (w2, bits 31-16) | Count loop-counter; if false 'RETURN'&amp;'HOLD'; if true use true specifications. | line 2 |
| `CONDENABL` | `000200` (w2, bits 31-16) | Enable conditional sequencing; use FALSE specs if condition is false. | line 3 |
| `SLWCS` | `002000` (w2, bits 31-16) | Start Load Writable Control Store. Avoid 'ROM-OUT-OF-RANGE'. | line 2 |
| `SEXT` | `001000` (w3, bits 47-32) | Standalone sign-extend modifier (bit 41). Normally combined with IDBS,GPR as the IDBS,GPR,SEXT composite; appears standalone on ND-100 microwords that use SEXT with a non-GPR IDBS source or with IDBS disabled. | line 2 |
| `EN_EXT` | `000004` (w4, bits 63-48) | Standalone XRF / Enable Extended Register File (bit 50). Normally bit 50 is embedded in composite A\_REG tokens such as A,SHCE; this token exists for microwords where bit 50 is asserted but no composite A-operand token matches. | line 1 |

### COMM

| Mnemonic | Bits | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COMM,ESRP` | `000010` (w3, bits 47-32) | Set 'R=P' flip-flop if 'F=0' is true. Detects store into prefetched next location. | line 2 |
| `COMM,EPIC` | `000011` (w3, bits 47-32) | A-operand is an instruction to PIC (Priority Interrupt Controller). | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,SMPID` | `000012` (w3, bits 47-32) | Set Micro-PID. PID positions where IDB has 1 are forced high (can only set, not clear). | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,START` | `000013` (w3, bits 47-32) | Reset the STOP flip-flop. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,SSTOP` | `000014` (w3, bits 47-32) | Set the STOP flip-flop. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,CLRTC` | `000015` (w3, bits 47-32) | Clear the 20ms clock flip-flop. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,CLFF` | `000016` (w3, bits 47-32) | Clear the OOD and the DZD flip-flops (floating-point rounding indicators). | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,LDLC` | `000017` (w3, bits 47-32) | Load the Loop Counter with the 6 lower IDB bits. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,LDPIL` | `000001` (w3, bits 47-32) | IDB bits 8-15 -&gt; STATUS bits 8-15. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,LDGPR` | `000002` (w3, bits 47-32) | IDB -&gt; General-Purpose Register. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,EWRF` | `000003` (w3, bits 47-32) | IDB -&gt; register file word addressed by A-operand and B-operand. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,CLIRQ` | `000004` (w3, bits 47-32) | Prevent jump to the interrupt vector; remove PANEL effect on IRQ test. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,RSDA` | `000005` (w3, bits 47-32) | Reset Data Available in UART. | line 2 |
| `COMM,TBSTR` | `000006` (w3, bits 47-32) | Transmit Buffer Strobe to UART. Lower IDB bits loaded into UART. | line 2 |
| `COMM,SIOC` | `000007` (w3, bits 47-32) | Load I/O-Control register, controlling terminal 1 and clock interrupts etc. | line 2, [runtime effect](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/nd-microcode-meta/docs/definitions/data-flow/#comm-effects) |
| `COMM,RDRQ` | `000034` (w3, bits 47-32) | Read memory request; address present on IDB. | line 2 |
| `COMM,WRRQ` | `000035` (w3, bits 47-32) | Write memory request; address present on IDB. | line 2 |
| `COMM,IDENT` | `000036` (w3, bits 47-32) | Start IDENT cycle on bus; address present on IDB. | line 2 |
| `COMM,IOX` | `000037` (w3, bits 47-32) | Start IOX cycle on bus; address present on bus. | line 2 |
| `COMM,IRDRQ` | `000030` (w3, bits 47-32) | Indirect address memory request; address on IDB. MIS selects paging mode. | line 2 |
| `COMM,DERQ` | `000031` (w3, bits 47-32) | Deposit memory request; address present on IDB. | line 2 |
| `COMM,EXRQ` | `000030` (w3, bits 47-32) | Examine memory request; address present on IDB. Same COMM code as IRDRQ with MIS=FETCH. | line 2, same as COMM,IRDRQ |
| `COMM,LDIR` | `000020` (w3, bits 47-32) | Load Interrupt Register Number into MMM (selects MMM register for subsequent access). | line 2 |
| `COMM,XMM` | `000021` (w3, bits 47-32) | Read/Write MMM register (previously selected by COMM,LDIR). | line 2 |

### T_SEQ

| Mnemonic | Bits | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `T,JMP` | all zero | True sequence is JMP. | line 2 |
| `T,JMP0-3` | `001000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is JMP. IR bits 0-3 control the four lower jump-address bits. | line 2 |
| `T,JMP8-10` | `002000` (w3, bits 47-32)<br>`001000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is JMP. IR bits 8-10 control the 3 lower jump-address bits. | line 2 |
| `T,JMPALD` | `004000` (w3, bits 47-32)<br>`001000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is JMP. ALD controls the 4 lower jump-address bits. | line 2 |
| `T,JMPAOPR` | `006000` (w3, bits 47-32)<br>`001000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is JMP. A-operand controls the 4 lower jump-address bits. | line 2 |
| `T,MAPJ` | `004000` (w2, bits 31-16) | If next microinstruction is JMP, the JMP will be mapped by the mapping hardware (bit 27 = MAPJ active). | line 2 |
| `T,RETURN` | `040000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is RETURN. | line 2 |
| `T,NEXT` | `100000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is NEXT. | line 2 |
| `T,REPEAT` | `140000` (w2, bits 31-16) | True sequence is REPEAT (T\_SEQ=0b11). Repeats the current microinstruction - used by multi-cycle operations. | line 2 |

### COND

| Mnemonic | Bits | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COND,STP` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000360` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is STOP (STP flip-flop). | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,OPCTT1` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000220` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is whether TT1 is on CPU board (MOPC terminal test for devices 0o300..0o307). | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,OVF` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000240` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is 'Overflow' from ALU bit-slices. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,CRY` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000260` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is 'Carry' from ALU bit-slices. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,F11` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000300` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is bit 11 from ALU bit-slices. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,F15` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000320` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is bit 15 (sign bit) from ALU bit-slices. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,F=0` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000340` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is 'All zeros' from ALU bit-slices. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,DR=2` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16) | Condition for testing is 'IR bits 0-2 = 010' (destination field = P). | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,LC=0` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000020` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is 'Loop counter content = 0'. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |
| `COND,FETCH` | `000400` (w2, bits 31-16)<br>`000100` (w1, bits 15-0) | Condition for testing is 'Last memory request was FETCH'. | line 3, provides [COND](#cond) |

    ```yaml
    # ==================================================================
    # AB (SYMBOLIC SCRATCH REGISTERS) - set both AOP and BOP simultaneously
    # ==================================================================
    # These tokens encode paired (AOP, BOP) values for addressing specific
    # scratch-word slots in the register file. Used by MOPC / panel / interrupt
    # routines. Each token sets w1 bits 12-15 (AOP) AND w2 bits 0-3 (BOP).
    ```
